symbols.name: \(n\)
symbols.def: Number of records on which \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\) are observed.

symbols.name: \(m\)
symbols.def: Number of independent records on which only \(X\) and \(A\) are observed.

symbols.name: \(d\)
symbols.def: Known number of discrete covariate categories.

symbols.name: \((m_n)_{n\ge1}\)
symbols.def: An arbitrary sequence of auxiliary sample sizes indexed by \(n\).

symbols.name: \((d_n)_{n\ge1}\)
symbols.def: An arbitrary sequence of covariate alphabet sizes indexed by \(n\).

symbols.name: \(\epsilon\)
symbols.def: Known fixed lower bound on occupied-cell treatment propensities.

symbols.name: \(x\)
symbols.def: Generic element of the known covariate alphabet.

symbols.name: \(Y\)
symbols.def: Binary gold-standard outcome, observed only in the labeled sample.

symbols.name: \(e_x\)
symbols.def: \(e_x=P(A=1\mid X=x)\) when \(p_x>0\), with an arbitrary fixed value when \(p_x=0\).

symbols.name: \(\mu_{ax}\)
symbols.def: \(\mu_{ax}=E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) on occupied treatment cells, with an arbitrary fixed value on null cells.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal T_{n,m,d}\)
symbols.def: All measurable estimators based on \(\mathcal L_n\) and \(\mathcal U_m\).

symbols.name: \(\Pi_0\)
symbols.def: Null prior to be derived from \(\mathrm{def:common-marginal-prior-handle}\).

symbols.name: \(\Pi_1\)
symbols.def: Alternative prior to be derived from \(\mathrm{def:common-marginal-prior-handle}\).

symbols.name: \(\Pi_0^{\mathrm{small}}\)
symbols.def: The null point mass in the finite calculation constructed in \(\mathrm{def:finite-small-instance}\).

symbols.name: \(\Pi_1^{\mathrm{small}}\)
symbols.def: The alternative point mass in the finite calculation constructed in \(\mathrm{def:finite-small-instance}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{small}}\)
symbols.def: The mixed-statistic and common-marginal calculation constructed in \(\mathrm{def:finite-small-instance}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{known}}_{n,d,\epsilon}\)
symbols.space: statistical experiments with deterministic side information
symbols.def: Experiment constructed in \(\mathrm{def:known-marginal-experiment}\), in which the exact table \(P_{XA}\) is supplied together with \(n\) complete records.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal T^{\mathrm{known}}_{n,d}\)
symbols.def: All measurable functions of \(\mathcal L_n\) and the exact supplied table \(P_{XA}\).

standard.name: independent and identically distributed labeled sampling

definitions.name: independent labeled and outcome-unlabeled experiment
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E_{n,m,d,\epsilon}:=\{P^{\otimes n}\otimes P_{XA}^{\otimes m}:P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon},\ n\ge1,\ m\ge0,\ d\ge2\}\), with the product coupling specified by \(\mathrm{ass:labeled-iid}\), \(\mathrm{ass:auxiliary-iid}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:sample-independence}\).

definitions.name: unequal-information annotation-frontier handle
definitions.construction: Determine an explicit elementary function \(r_\epsilon(n,m,d)\) by optimizing the approximation degree and heavy--light threshold when each admissible monomial contains at most one outcome-marked factor estimated from \(\mathcal L_n\), while all remaining treatment--mass factorial factors are estimated from the pooled \(N=n+m\) treatment--covariate records; the expression must be capped for every \(n,m,d\) and contain no optimization over \(P\).

definitions.name: mixed marked--unmarked polynomial hybrid handle
definitions.construction: Construct \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}\) by an independent pooled-count pilot that separates light and heavy \((X,A)\) cells, a near-best reciprocal polynomial on the light branch whose factorial lift is linear in \(q_{ax}\) and uses higher powers only of \(s_{ax}\), an inverse-count outcome mean on the heavy branch, mass-weighted aggregation across \(x\), and final clipping to \([-1,1]\); derive all tuning constants from \(n,m,d,\epsilon\) alone.

definitions.name: auxiliary-invariant fuzzy-hypothesis handle
definitions.construction: Construct \(\Pi_0\) and \(\Pi_1\) by best-polynomial-approximation duality so that they induce exactly the same random \(P_{XA}\), separate \(\tau(P)\) only through conditional outcome marks, match every likelihood monomial through the chosen degree whenever it contains a labeled mark, and are normalized into \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) with a reservoir cell before transfer from independent Poisson counts to the fixed \((n,m)\) experiment.

definitions.name: finite mixed-statistic and common-marginal calculation
definitions.construction: Let \(\epsilon=1/4\), \(d=2\), \(p_1=p_2=1/2\), \(e_1=e_2=1/2\), and \(\mu_{01}=\mu_{02}=0\). For \(n=m=1\), independence of the samples gives \[E\!\left[2\mathbf 1\{\mathcal L_1=((1,1,1))\}\left(\mathbf 1\{\mathcal U_1=((1,0))\}+\mathbf 1\{\mathcal U_1=((1,1))\}\right)\right]=2q_{11}p_1.\] At \(\mu_{11}=1\), this equals \(1/4\), while the treated cell target is \(p_1\mu_{11}=1/2\). Define \(\Pi_0^{\mathrm{small}}\) to put unit mass on the law with \(\mu_{11}=\mu_{12}=0\), and define \(\Pi_1^{\mathrm{small}}\) to put unit mass on the law with \(\mu_{11}=1\) and \(\mu_{12}=0\). Under both priors, \(P_{XA}(x,a)=1/4\) for all \((x,a)\), whereas \(\tau(P)=0\) under \(\Pi_0^{\mathrm{small}}\) and \(\tau(P)=1/2\) under \(\Pi_1^{\mathrm{small}}\); consequently the auxiliary laws agree for every \(m\), and the total variation distance between the two labeled laws is \(1-(3/4)^n\). These identities constitute \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{small}}\).

definitions.name: known-treatment--covariate-marginal experiment
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{known}}_{n,d,\epsilon}:=\{(P^{\otimes n},P_{XA}):P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon},\ n\ge1,\ d\ge2\}\), where the first coordinate generates \(\mathcal L_n\) and the second coordinate is the exact \(2d\)-cell table observed as deterministic side information.

statements.statement: There exist \(0<c_\epsilon\le C_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, uniformly for \(n\ge1\) and \(d\ge2\), \[\frac{c_\epsilon}{n}\le R_\epsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(n,d)\le\frac{C_\epsilon}{n}.\]
statements.justification: This is the limiting benchmark when the auxiliary sample reveals all treatment and mass information but supplies no outcomes.
statements.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 5, shows that knowing \(P_X\) alone can leave constant risk; exact knowledge of \(P_{XA}\) also reveals the propensity and changes that conclusion.
statements.consumer: The benchmark determines the maximum possible return from acquiring additional treatment--covariate records.

statements.statement: Can the construction obtained from \(\mathrm{def:mixed-estimator-handle}\) be made total and computable and satisfy, for constants depending only on \(\epsilon\), \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}E_{P^{\otimes n}\otimes P_{XA}^{\otimes m}}[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}-\tau(P))^2]\le C_\epsilon r_\epsilon(n,m,d)\] simultaneously for every \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\), with a proof that controls false-light polynomial tails, random branch means, and mass-weighted covariance summation without a factor in \(d\) or \(m/n\)?
statements.justification: This isolates the first genuinely changed upper-bound step: outcome marks have budget \(n\), while unmarked factorial moments have budget \(n+m\).
statements.gap: JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015 and WuYang2016 lift every monomial factor from one sample, while ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 uses labeled four-cell counts. The finite calculation in \(\mathrm{def:finite-small-instance}\) already requires one outcome-marked factor from \(\mathcal L_n\) and a separate marginal factor from \(\mathcal U_m\); none of the comparators proves the resulting unequal-information hybrid-risk lemma.
statements.consumer: The resulting estimator gives a model-free discrete benchmark for allocating chart-review outcomes in the ChengAnanthakrishnanCai2021 setting.

statements.statement: Can the priors obtained from \(\mathrm{def:common-marginal-prior-handle}\) be normalized and transferred to the fixed two-sample experiment so that they induce identical auxiliary laws and imply \[R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\ge c_\epsilon r_\epsilon(n,m,d)\] for every \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\), including the capped constant-risk regime?
statements.justification: A supervised lower prior that perturbs \(P_{XA}\) is detected by the auxiliary sample, so exact marginal invariance is the essential new converse mechanism.
statements.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Appendix C.5, randomizes treatment and mass parameters in a one-sample fuzzy hypothesis; WuYang2016 provides approximation duality but not the auxiliary-invariance constraint or the two-sample normalization transfer. The two point masses in \(\mathrm{def:finite-small-instance}\) verify exact \(P_{XA}\) agreement and label-gated discrepancy in a finite experiment, but their total variation is too large to supply the all-regime frontier.
statements.consumer: The lower bound prevents chart-review planning from treating unlabeled records as if they also supplied outcome-bearing moments.

statements.statement: Determine a closed numerical expression for \(r_\epsilon(n,m,d)\), with no unknown-law optimization, for which \[c_\epsilon r_\epsilon(n,m,d)\le R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\le C_\epsilon r_\epsilon(n,m,d)\] holds uniformly over all \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\). As the required supervised endpoint reduction, prove \[r_\epsilon(n,0,d)\asymp_\epsilon\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\},\] the matched rate recorded in \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap}\), without treating that endpoint as a new result. For the benchmark experiment \(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{known}}_{n,d,\epsilon}\), prove the exact fixed-parameter limit \[\lim_{m\to\infty}R_\epsilon(n,m,d)=R_\epsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(n,d)\qquad\text{for every fixed }n\ge1\text{ and }d\ge2.\] Along every sequence \(n\to\infty\), give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions written only as elementary limits or inequalities in \(n\), \(m_n\), and \(d_n\), with no shorthand through \(r_\epsilon\), for each of \(R_\epsilon(n,m_n,d_n)\to0\), \(R_\epsilon(n,m_n,d_n)=O(n^{-1})\), and the strict order improvement \(R_\epsilon(n,m_n,d_n)=o\{R_\epsilon(n,0,d_n)\}\).
statements.justification: The matched all-regime rate is the theorem-level kernel: it makes the number of treatment-only records a quantitative information parameter and must certify an order-changing, not merely monotone, value of annotation.
statements.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 and the catalogued \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap}\) result resolve the supervised obstruction, while ChengAnanthakrishnanCai2021, ChakraborttyDai2024, and Kato2025 provide regular semi-supervised efficiency statements. The requested result strictly refines the supervised boundary into a two-sample frontier by recovering it at \(m=0\), proving the fixed-\((n,d)\) limit to the explicitly defined known-\(P_{XA}\) experiment, and characterizing exactly when auxiliary records change the minimax order.
statements.consumer: Sections 2.1 and 4 of ChengAnanthakrishnanCai2021 gain a baseline-only decision rule for comparing another chart-reviewed outcome with another treatment--covariate record when working nuisance models are not trusted.

sampling_model.design: Two independent samples from one population: \(\mathcal L_n\sim P^{\otimes n}\) and \(\mathcal U_m\sim P_{XA}^{\otimes m}\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\ge1\) labeled records and \(m\ge0\) outcome-unlabeled records with \(X\in[d]\).
sampling_model.overlap: The fixed known constant satisfies \(0<\epsilon<1/2\); no minimum \(p_x\) is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Neither \(p_x\), \(e_x\), nor \(\mu_{ax}\) is known. The estimator handle uses labeled outcome marks and pooled treatment--mass factorial moments with separate information budgets.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 gives the supervised lower scale \(n^{-1}+d^2/(n^2\log^2 n)\), and Theorem 5 shows that knowing \(P_X\) alone can leave constant minimax risk.
The paper gives robust and locally efficient semi-supervised ATE estimation using a small chart-reviewed sample and a much larger EHR cohort.
Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.1 give an asymptotic expansion and root-\(n\) normality under explicit nuisance-error controls in the labeled--unlabeled experiment.
The two-sample results derive regular efficient influence functions and an attaining asymptotically normal estimator under support and nuisance-rate conditions.
The paper constructs minimax estimators by applying factorial-moment polynomial estimation on rare cells and a bias-corrected plug-in rule on regular cells.
Theorem 1 matches entropy upper and lower rates through best polynomial approximation and its moment-matching dual.

tldr: Gold-standard outcomes may be available only for \(n\) chart-reviewed records even though treatment and baseline covariates are available for another \(m\) records. The research kernel is the sharp finite-sample minimax MSE over every \((n,m,d)\) regime, delivered through three open questions: a mixed marked--unmarked polynomial upper bound, an exactly common-\(P_{XA}\) converse, and their matched annotation frontier. A finite \(d=2\), \(\epsilon=1/4\) calculation shows a statistic multiplying a labeled outcome mark by an independent marginal factor and two hypotheses with identical auxiliary laws but different ATEs. The frontier must recover the catalogued supervised rate only as its \(m=0\) endpoint, prove convergence to the explicitly defined known-\(P_{XA}\) risk for each fixed \((n,d)\) as \(m\to\infty\), and give explicit necessary and sufficient thresholds for consistency, root-\(n\) MSE, and strict order improvement.

project_justification.gap: Supervised discrete ATE theory identifies a logarithmic rare-cell barrier, whereas semi-supervised causal papers establish regular local efficiency under nuisance consistency or working models. Neither literature quantifies the joint finite-sample experiment in which outcome-bearing information has size \(n\) and treatment--mass information has size \(n+m\), with null cells and unrestricted regression functions; the standard adjustment identity and Blackwell monotonicity do not answer that quantitative question.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is an annotation frontier that is uniform in \(n,m,d\), respects the different information budgets inside each polynomial monomial, and uses lower priors invisible to every auxiliary observation rather than recycling a supervised prior.
project_justification.fill: The three focal open questions seek a total mixed-factorial heavy--light estimator, an exactly common-\(P_{XA}\) fuzzy-hypothesis converse, and one matching numerical rate. The rate must reproduce the catalogued supervised formula at \(m=0\), converge to the formally defined known-\(P_{XA}\) risk for fixed \((n,d)\), and yield explicit necessary and sufficient inequalities in \(n,m_n,d_n\) for consistency, parametric MSE, and strict order improvement.

related_work: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, \cite{ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024}, Theorem 2 and Appendix C.5, derive the supervised moment-matching obstruction; their Theorem 5 and Appendix C.9 show why knowledge of \(P_X\) does not reveal the propensity. The matched supervised rate is recorded in the in-catalogue result \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap}\) and enters only as the required \(m=0\) endpoint, not as a solve target or contribution. Cheng, Ananthakrishnan, and Cai, \cite{ChengAnanthakrishnanCai2021}, Sections 2.1 and 4, supply the chart-review motivation and a robust locally efficient estimator that leverages outcome surrogates; the present target is only a baseline discrete benchmark and does not claim their surrogate efficiency. Chakrabortty and Dai, \cite{ChakraborttyDai2024}, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.1, derive a two-sample expansion whose root-\(n\) conclusion depends on propensity and regression error rates. Kato, \cite{Kato2025}, Theorems 4.2 and 4.4, gives the adjacent regular two-stratum efficiency theory under fixed sample fractions and nuisance conditions. Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman, \cite{JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015}, Sections I-A and III, motivate the rare-cell polynomial versus smooth-cell split and coefficient-sensitive factorial analysis. Wu and Yang, \cite{WuYang2016}, Theorem 1 and Appendix E, supply the best-approximation and moment-matching duality used to enforce the new common-marginal converse. The finite calculation \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{small}}\) separates these roles concretely: its mixed statistic uses an outcome mark from \(\mathcal L_1\) and a marginal factor from \(\mathcal U_1\), while its two hypotheses agree exactly on every auxiliary observation. None of these sources states an all-regime minimax rate for the present unequal-information ATE experiment or the fixed-\((n,d)\) convergence of its risk to the known-\(P_{XA}\) experiment.
technical_internal_limitation: The finite calculation \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{small}}\) is diagnostic rather than a rate theorem. Its mixed statistic has expectation \(2q_{11}p_1=1/4\) in the displayed law, so the approximation bias is visible against the treated-cell target \(1/2\); the full hybrid must choose a higher degree and control its tails. Its two common-\(P_{XA}\) point masses have labeled total variation \(1-(3/4)^n\), so a moment-matched fuzzy refinement is required for a sharp lower bound. Neither mechanism follows by replacing \(n\) with \(n+m\) in a supervised construction: that substitution would estimate \(q_{ax}\), an outcome-marked mass, from records without \(Y\), and a supervised prior that changes \(P_{XA}\) becomes distinguishable as \(m\) grows. The presolve candidate \(\min\{1,n^{-1}+[d/\{(n+m)\log(en)\}]^2\}\) remains diagnostic evidence only because the false-light tail bound, branch-mean variance, normalization of the common-marginal lower prior, and fixed-sample transfers are unproved.
honest_scope: Under consistency, conditional exchangeability, and occupied-cell overlap, the standard setup identity is \(E[Y(1)-Y(0)]=\tau(P)=\sum_{x=1}^{d}p_x(\mu_{1x}-\mu_{0x})\), including null cells. As an unnumbered Blackwell sanity check, \(R_\epsilon(n,m+1,d)\le R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\) and \(R_\epsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(n,d)\le R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\le R_\epsilon(n,0,d)\). The matched supervised rate from \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap}\) is solely the required \(m=0\) reduction. The known-marginal benchmark means the experiment that supplies the exact table \(P_{XA}\) as deterministic side information, and the only limit asserted for it is the open fixed-\((n,d)\) claim \(\lim_{m\to\infty}R_\epsilon(n,m,d)=R_\epsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(n,d)\); no triangular-array version is presumed. The exact finite-\(m\) rate, its explicit strict-separation threshold, the uniform hybrid-risk lemma, and the auxiliary-invariant lower-bound transfer are open. The project assumes neither smoothness, sparsity, effect homogeneity, outcome surrogacy, a minimum cell mass, nor selected enrollment. It does not provide confidence intervals, optimize nonuniform validation probabilities, or validate the ChengAnanthakrishnanCai2021 empirical data under this unrestricted model.

seed_details.seed: Characterize the exact finite-sample minimax MSE in the independent \(n\)-labeled, \(m\)-unlabeled experiment by a mixed-factorial upper bound and an exactly common-\(P_{XA}\) converse.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction, Theorem 2, Appendix C.5, Theorem 5, Appendix C.9, and Section 8
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace the one-budget four-cell factorial lift by a one-mark lift with labeled budget \(n\) and unmarked budget \(n+m\); replace the supervised fuzzy hypothesis by priors agreeing exactly on \(P_{XA}\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for semi-supervised discrete ATE minimax risk and unequal labeled--unlabeled functional estimation found regular expansions but no all-regime match.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Immediate from the supervised rate after replacing \(n\) by \(n+m\).
seed_details.rebuttal: Outcome marks still have only \(n\) observations, and every supervised prior that perturbs \(P_{XA}\) becomes detectable by the auxiliary sample.

seed_details.seed: Characterize the minimax information lattice for auxiliary \(X\), auxiliary \((X,A)\), known \(P_X\), known \(e_x\), and known \(P_{XA}\).
seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction contribution 4, Theorem 5, equations 14 and 15, Appendix C.9, and Section 8
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Impose the appropriate exact marginal agreement constraint on each lower prior and derive separate polynomial lifts for each observed auxiliary field.
seed_details.destination_search: ChakraborttyDai2024 compares treatment-observed and treatment-unobserved auxiliaries asymptotically, while Kato2025 treats regular strata; neither supplies uniform minimax equivalence classes.
seed_details.cynical_objection: The lattice is only a table of obvious Blackwell orderings.
seed_details.rebuttal: The open content is the explicit rate-equivalence and strict-separation frontier, not monotonicity, and Zeng's known-\(P_X\) obstruction shows that variable content changes the rate nontrivially.

seed_details.seed: Derive the maximal growing-alphabet regime in which the regular two-stratum efficiency bound remains attainable, and the first regime in which rare-cell bias forces a nonregular limit.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction, Theorem 2.1, Corollary 2.1, proof remainder decomposition, and Section 7
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace abstract nuisance-rate assumptions by exact multinomial occupancy calculations and compare the efficient-score remainder with the rare-cell approximation modulus.
seed_details.destination_search: Kato2025 derives two-stratum efficiency under fixed fractions and product-rate conditions; ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 gives a supervised plug-in CLT only in its regular regime.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This is a direct specialization of published semiparametric efficiency theory to indicator regressors.
seed_details.rebuttal: Published efficiency theorems assume the nuisance remainder is small; deriving the exact occupancy boundary and proving failure beyond it is the missing converse direction.

seed_details.seed: Obtain the limit-law phase diagram for a mixed polynomial ATE estimator, including Gaussian, biased-Gaussian, and non-Gaussian rare-cell regimes.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Appendix A, Theorem 8 and its influence-function proof, contrasted with Theorem 2 and Section 8
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace the low-dimensional influence-function expansion by a triangular-array analysis of mixed marked--unmarked polynomial cell contributions.
seed_details.destination_search: ChakraborttyDai2024 and Kato2025 provide regular Gaussian limits only after nuisance-rate assumptions; no mixed-polynomial non-Gaussian limit was located.
seed_details.cynical_objection: A central limit theorem follows from independent Poisson cell summands.
seed_details.rebuttal: The data-dependent branch, non-negligible approximation bias, de-Poissonization, and possibly dominant rare cells invalidate an automatic Lindeberg argument.

seed_details.seed: Determine the semi-supervised minimax frontier under a shrinking bound on cell-effect heterogeneity.
seed_details.anchor_locator: honest scope and the reviewer strengthening path on the shrinking-radius wedge
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Recompute the signed one-mark covariance with pooled unmarked factorial factors and enforce the heterogeneity radius under common-\(P_{XA}\) lower priors.
seed_details.destination_search: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 covers homogeneous and unrestricted supervised endpoints, but no semi-supervised shrinking-radius interior was located.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This only appends \(m\) to an already unresolved supervised wedge.
seed_details.rebuttal: The unequal-information sample changes the competing branches asymmetrically, but the inherited unresolved wedge makes this a weaker first angle.

seed_details.seed: Construct honest confidence intervals with optimal worst-case expected length across the annotation transition.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Appendix A, Theorem 8, and the large-alphabet MSE results in Theorems 1 and 2
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace second-moment bounds by uniform tail control and an explicit approximation-bias radius for the mixed polynomial estimator.
seed_details.destination_search: Regular semi-supervised Wald intervals appear in ChakraborttyDai2024 and Kato2025, but no honest rare-cell confidence-length frontier was located.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Bias-aware critical values are immediate once an MSE bound is known.
seed_details.rebuttal: MSE does not provide uniform coverage, a sharp bias radius, a variance estimator, or a matching expected-length lower bound in the two-sample experiment.

seed_details.seed: Choose cell-dependent outcome-validation probabilities under a labeling-cost constraint and certify the minimax optimal design-estimator pair.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction chart-review motivation, Section 2.1 setup, Section 4 EHR analysis, and Discussion
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace oracle influence-function variance allocation by a saddle criterion combining assignment-dependent variance with worst-case rare-cell approximation bias.
seed_details.destination_search: Classical two-phase design optimizes regular variance using pilot moments; no pilot-free large-alphabet minimax validation allocation was located.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Neyman allocation solves the labeling design after plugging in conditional variances.
seed_details.rebuttal: Without minimum masses or uniformly consistent pilots, rare-cell bias is absent from Neyman allocation and the oracle conditional variances cannot be treated as known.

seed_details.seed: Use the auxiliary cohort to learn a treatment policy with welfare regret controlled by annotation cost.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: A policy class and empirical welfare criterion would have to replace fixed-ATE squared error.
seed_details.destination_search: The supplied experiment contains no policy class, feasibility constraint, or welfare target, so a destination theorem would require a new problem rather than a changed proof step.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This changes the estimand from a fixed ATE to policy welfare and is not an annotation-frontier result.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds in the supplied model.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The M16 lane has a named obstruction: no policy decision class or welfare loss is present.

seed_details.seed: Invert a label-permutation or conformal symmetry to obtain finite-sample ATE confidence sets.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Section 2 observation model and Appendix A sampling-based inference
seed_details.changed_proof_step: A group action leaving the counterfactual null distribution invariant would have to replace the sampling CLT.
seed_details.destination_search: Independent observational sampling with exchangeability conditional on \(X\) does not create a treatment permutation group, and random outcome labeling alone does not reveal missing potential outcomes.
seed_details.cynical_objection: There is no exact symmetry orbit for the causal null in this observational experiment.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds without adding a randomized treatment design or a structural prediction model.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The M17 lane has a named obstruction: random labeling is not random treatment assignment and supplies no counterfactual permutation symmetry.

literature_map.settled: The supervised experiment has a logarithmic rare-cell obstruction, and the in-catalogue \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap}\) result records the matched \(m=0\) rate used here only as an endpoint reduction.
literature_map.open_boundary: The proof does not allocate different sample sizes to outcome marks and treatment--mass factors, and its lower prior need not preserve \(P_{XA}\).

literature_map.settled: Robustness, influence-function efficiency, and Gaussian limits are available under working models, nuisance convergence, support conditions, or fixed sample fractions.
literature_map.open_boundary: These local results do not give worst-case finite-alphabet risk with null cells or an arbitrary \(m/n\) ratio.

literature_map.settled: Rare-cell best-polynomial estimation, factorial-moment lifting, Poissonization, and approximation-duality lower bounds are established for one-budget discrete functionals.
literature_map.open_boundary: The target requires monomials with one labeled mark and several pooled unmarked factors, plus dual priors constrained to have an identical auxiliary marginal.

novelty_justification.closest_results: The closest theorem is ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2, and the matched supervised endpoint is recorded by the in-catalogue \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap}\) result; the closest observation design is ChakraborttyDai2024, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.1, for regular two-sample estimation.
novelty_justification.strict_delta: The focal object is a uniform finite-sample rate in three information parameters. It must recover the catalogued supervised rate solely at \(m=0\), prove \(\lim_{m\to\infty}R_\epsilon(n,m,d)=R_\epsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(n,d)\) for every fixed \((n,d)\), and give explicit necessary and sufficient inequalities in \(n,m_n,d_n\) for consistency, root-\(n\) MSE, and \(R_\epsilon(n,m_n,d_n)=o\{R_\epsilon(n,0,d_n)\}\). The standard adjustment identity and weak Blackwell monotonicity are setup checks, not contributions. Neither theorem-level comparator contains this two-sample rate, a one-mark mixed factorial lift, or a lower prior invisible to auxiliary \((X,A)\) observations.

When unlabeled treatment records rescue causal estimation: the sharp annotation frontier. Fix known 0<epsilon<1/2. Observe n>=1 independent labeled records (X,A,Y) distributed as P and m>=0 independent unlabeled records (X,A) distributed as its SAME marginal P_XA, independent of the labeled sample. X is in the known alphabet [d], d>=2; A and Y are binary. All cell probabilities p_x>=0 summing to one are allowed, including null cells; epsilon<=e_x=P(A=1|X=x)<=1-epsilon on occupied cells; mu_ax=P(Y=1|A=a,X=x) is unrestricted in [0,1]. Neither p nor e is known. No smoothness, sparsity, effect homogeneity, outcome surrogacy, or minimum cell mass is assumed. Consistency and conditional exchangeability identify tau(P)=sum_x p_x(mu_1x-mu_0x). The target population is shared by both samples, and missing outcomes are by independent random labeling, not selected enrollment. Determine, up to constants depending only on epsilon, the minimax MSE R_epsilon(n,m,d)=inf_T sup_P E_(P^n x P_XA^m)[(T-tau(P))^2] over all measurable estimators, uniformly for n>=1,m>=0,d>=2. Exhibit a numerical rate r_epsilon(n,m,d) with no unspecified optimization over unknown laws, prove a total computable estimator attaining it and a matching lower bound in the same observation experiment for every regime. Derive necessary and sufficient growth conditions for R->0 and R=O(1/n) along arbitrary n->infinity sequences m_n,d_n. The sharp tradeoff must include the m=0 frontier, the finite-m transition, and the limiting known-propensity benchmark. Leave the exact rate formula open; do not obtain it by substituting n+m for n in the supervised rate. The new theorem is the unequal-information approximation/variance and indistinguishability frontier: outcome-bearing moments have n observations, while treatment/mass information has n+m. Consumer: Cheng, Ananthakrishnan and Cai, Biometrics 2021, Robust and efficient semi-supervised estimation of average treatment effects with application to electronic health records data, Sections 2.1 and 4 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7758040/). Their IBD comparative-effectiveness study observes treatment/covariates in all records but validates outcomes through random chart review. The frontier supplies a baseline-only discrete-adjustment benchmark for choosing additional chart labels versus acquiring treatment-covariate records when working nuisance models are not trusted. It does not claim efficiency with their post-treatment surrogates or validate that data set under an unrestricted discrete model. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolve derived an inverse-count baseline and a mixed Chebyshev approximation linear in outcome-bearing masses, allowing one labeled factor and many treatment-only factorial factors. A signed prior preserves the entire marginal distribution of cell masses and propensities while changing conditional outcome marks; auxiliary-only observations then agree exactly, and the joint likelihood discrepancy requires labeled observations. Symbolic polynomial identities, ten finite-atom priors and nine joint-likelihood checks passed. The suggested rate min{1,1/n+[d/((n+m)log(en))]^2} remains conjectural; the original problem stays answer-open. Known-propensity, m=0, d=2, null-cell and large-m boundaries were checked, without claiming the complete theorem.

Recheck the joint-prior likelihood and normalization cost. If these fail, restart the answer derivation within the original model rather than asserting the proposed rate or substituting a weaker theorem.
